title: Environment
description: The research:environment block in research/ENVIRONMENT.md — what the lab can and cannot measure. It is the file a Day-1 criterion reads: an infeasible experiment has to land here as a limitation, distinct from a scientific negative. Until this schema existed the block was read by nothing and never validated, so a limitation that never got written and a limitation nobody checked looked the same.

available.description: What the lab actually has, by namespace.

limitations.description: Capabilities the environment does not support. A limitation is not a result: it says the question cannot be measured here, which is why it is kept apart from a refuted hypothesis.

harnesses.description: Surrogates the lab does have, and what each one preserves and drops. This is the environment's half of the surrogate contract: the record states the boundary for one claim, the harness states it once for every claim that uses it.

capability_map.description: Research capabilities the lab tracks for investment judgement (V1 §3.1 #17, Block 1.5 / P4). Each entry carries the strongest evidence level it has been used at and a reuse_counter that records how often it has been cited. Written by `env declare capability_map <file>`; see docs/design/CAPABILITY_MAP_SHAPE_PROPOSAL.md for the full rationale and dropped alternatives.

capability.description: What this entry is about, in one short line.

status.description: AVAILABLE — capability is real and the lab can use it. LIMITED — capability is real but degraded or partial. UNSUPPORTED — capability does not exist here (mirrors the harness/limitation dichotomy). For UNSUPPORTED entries, a parallel limitations[] entry should exist.

supports_evidence.description: Strongest evidence level this capability has been used at. Optional until first use. The original proposal (§2 of CAPABILITY_MAP_SHAPE_PROPOSAL.md) restricted this to E2|E3|null on the grounds that capability_map is a post-surrogate investment judgement; in practice E0 / E1 entries also exist (a capability can be visible from an env_blocked receipt before any surrogate runs), so the enum follows the full evidence-level scale.

reuse_counter.description: How many evidence records cite this capability. Zero is allowed (declared speculatively, never reused).

first_used_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of the first cite. Null until then. No format-level constraint — the validator does not implement `format` and a permissive pattern would enforce nothing.

last_used_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of the most recent cite. Null until first use.

last_used_by_evidence_id.description: The evidence_id of the record that bumped reuse_counter most recently.

notes.description: Free-form short prose. Absent-by-default; the validator treats missing and null as equivalent.
